pr.title: [beta] backports
pr.description:
- Bump libc to 0.2.161 #131823
- Avoid use imports in `thread_local_inner!` #131866
- Mark `simplify_aggregate_to_copy` mir-opt as unsound #132356

r? cuviper
pr.author: cuviper

analysis.originalLogic: GVN's `simplify_aggregate_to_copy` optimization rewrites construction of an aggregate `Rvalue` (specifically `AggregateTy::Def`) into a copy of an already-computed equivalent aggregate value. In `gvn.rs` the original code was: `if let AggregateTy::Def(_, _) = ty && let Some(value) = self.simplify_aggregate_to_copy(rvalue, location, &fields, variant_index) { ... }`. The optimization assumes a previously seen aggregate value can safely be reused as a copy at the current location.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical transformation was unsound: it reused a previously computed aggregate by inserting copies/dereferences of a place without checking whether intervening writes invalidated aliasing. In the demonstrated miscompile MIR, GVN replaced the dereference chain `_11 = deref_copy (*_4); _3 = &(*_11);` with `_11 = copy _1; _3 = &(*_1);` and replaced construction `_0 = Option::<i32>::Some(move _9);` with `_0 = copy (*_2);` after the program had executed `(*_1) = const Option::<i32>::None;`. Because `_2` aliases the mutated `*_1`/`*_v`, the copy reads the overwritten `None` instead of the originally observed `Some(col)`. The PR comment describes the cause as the optimization "introduce[d] new dereferences without checking for aliasing".
analysis.inputDomain: MIR optimized by GVN (at `-O`/non-zero opt-level) for Rust programs that (a) construct an aggregate, e.g. `Option::Some(col)` or a struct, from a value/borrow obtained through an alias, and (b) subsequently mutate the same underlying place through an aliasing `&mut` reference before the aggregate value is used. The miscompile tests use `&mut Option<i32>`, `if let &Some(col) = get(&v)`, then `*v = None; return Some(col);`, plus a `Vec<Option<usize>>` release/debug variant. It is exercised only with the `-Zunsound-mir-opts` gate after this PR.
analysis.summary: Historical bug-fix PR marks GVN's `simplify_aggregate_to_copy` MIR optimization as unsound because it rewrites aggregate construction into a copy of an aliasing place, introducing new dereferences without aliasing checks, so a later write through an alias can change the value read. The fix gates the optimization behind `-Zunsound-mir-opts`. Reusable knowledge: when testing GVN copy/aggregate canonicalization, check that any reused aggregate value is not invalidated by intervening mutable aliasing.
analysis.trigger: GVN sees an aggregate `Rvalue` (`AggregateTy::Def`) that it can canonicalize to an existing aggregate value while there exists a live alias to the place that is written between the original read and the replacement copy. In the minimized case: read `Some(col)` out of `&Option<i32>`, overwrite `*v = None`, then return `Some(col)`; GVN instead emits `copy (*_2)` after the overwrite, reading `None`.
preconditions: Function is compiled with non-zero optimization (`-O` / `-C opt-level=1`), so MIR GVN runs.
The unsound sub-optimization is enabled; after this PR it requires `-Zunsound-mir-opts`, e.g. `//@ compile-flags: -O -Zunsound-mir-opts`.
An aggregate is constructed from a value/borrow reached through an alias.
The same underlying place is later mutated through a mutable alias before the aggregate is consumed.
The pre-Some field is read before the mutation, but the canonicalized copy is placed after it.
pitfalls: Reusing a previously computed aggregate value is only valid if its provenance and contents are unchanged at the reuse point; do not conflate "same value expression" with "same value at a later program point".
Introducing new dereferences (`deref_copy`, `copy (*_place)`) changes when the memory is read and can expose aliasing bugs.
Borrowing restrictions and post-copy overwrites are separate conditions: the bug requires the overwrite to dominate the inserted copy, not merely the existence of a borrow.
The failure is opt-level dependent: observed as a panic in release/opt-level 1 but not at opt-level 0 (debug), so a debug-only test will not exercise GVN's reuse.
Do not infer conclusions from retained test names or old comments; compare actual value assignments (`_0 = Option::<i32>::Some(move _9)` vs `_0 = copy (*_2)`) in the decoded MIR revisions.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused MIR test (`tests/mir-opt/simplify_aggregate_to_copy_miscompile.rs`) using `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN`, `//@ compile-flags: -O -Zunsound-mir-opts`, `#![feature(rustc_attrs, core_intrinsics)]`, a `#[no_mangle] #[inline(never)] #[rustc_nounwind] fn get` returning `&Option<i32>`, and `// EMIT_MIR simplify_aggregate_to_copy_miscompile.foo.GVN.diff` to pin the before/after MIR. Add a `run-pass` UI regression with `release` (`-C opt-level=1`) and `debug` (`-C opt-level=0`) revisions that asserts the returned `Option` is `Some`. Gate existing GVN/codegen clone-as-copy tests with `-Zunsound-mir-opts` and a FIXME link. Inspect the decoded MIR to assert the unsound rewrite (post-overwrite `copy (*_2)`) is absent once the optimization is fixed.
evidence: > introduce[d] new dereferences without checking for aliasing
// Note: it's not strictly cargo's release profile, but any non-zero opt-level was sufficient to
// panic happened on 1.83.0 beta in release mode but not debug mode.
